title: Stripe API — Payment Intents
overview: Subset of the official Stripe OpenAPI spec (spec3.sdk.json) covering the core Payment Intents lifecycle: create, retrieve, update, confirm, cancel, capture. Stripe is a REST API; request bodies are application/x-www-form-urlencoded and successful responses return the PaymentIntent object. Authentication uses the secret API key via HTTP Bearer (or HTTP Basic with the key as username).

security_schemes.name: bearerAuth
security_schemes.details: Bearer HTTP authentication. Allowed headers-- Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

security_schemes.name: basicAuth
security_schemes.details: Basic HTTP authentication. Allowed headers-- Authorization: Basic <api_key> | Authorization: Basic <base64 hash of `api_key:`>

schemas.name: payment_intent

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the object.

fields.name: object
fields.description: String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).

fields.name: amount_received
fields.description: Amount that this PaymentIntent collects.

fields.name: currency
fields.description: Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Status of this PaymentIntent, one of `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `requires_capture`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`. Read more about each PaymentIntent [status](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses).

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description:
The client secret of this PaymentIntent. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key. 

The client secret can be used to complete a payment from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the customer. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret.

Refer to our docs to [accept a payment](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment?ui=elements) and learn about how `client_secret` should be handled.

fields.name: customer
fields.description:
ID of the Customer this PaymentIntent belongs to, if one exists.

Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this PaymentIntent.

If [setup_future_usage](https://api.stripe.com#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) is set and this PaymentIntent's payment method is not `card_present`, then the payment method attaches to the Customer after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card is created and attached to the Customer instead.

fields.name: payment_method
fields.description: ID of the payment method used in this PaymentIntent.

fields.name: payment_method_types
fields.description: The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this PaymentIntent is allowed to use. A comprehensive list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).

fields.name: capture_method
fields.description: Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account.

fields.name: confirmation_method
fields.description: Describes whether we can confirm this PaymentIntent automatically, or if it requires customer action to confirm the payment.

fields.name: created
fields.description: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

fields.name: description
fields.description: An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.

fields.name: latest_charge
fields.description: ID of the latest [Charge object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges) created by this PaymentIntent. This property is `null` until PaymentIntent confirmation is attempted.

fields.name: next_action
fields.description: If present, this property tells you what actions you need to take in order for your customer to fulfill a payment using the provided source.

fields.name: receipt_email
fields.description: Email address that the receipt for the resulting payment will be sent to. If `receipt_email` is specified for a payment in live mode, a receipt will be sent regardless of your [email settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/emails).

fields.name: setup_future_usage
fields.description:
Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.

If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.

If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.

When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Learn more about [storing information in metadata](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/creating-payment-intents#storing-information-in-metadata).

fields.name: livemode
fields.description: If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.

schemas.constraints:
A PaymentIntent guides you through the process of collecting a payment from your customer.
We recommend that you create exactly one PaymentIntent for each order or
customer session in your system. You can reference the PaymentIntent later to
see the history of payment attempts for a particular session.

A PaymentIntent transitions through
[multiple statuses](/payments/paymentintents/lifecycle)
throughout its lifetime as it interfaces with Stripe.js to perform
authentication flows and ultimately creates at most one successful charge.

Related guide: [Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents)

Basic HTTP authentication. Allowed headers-- Authorization: Basic <api_key> | Authorization: Basic <base64 hash of `api_key:`>

missing: Per-operation error responses / status codes are not captured in this subset (Stripe uses a global error object schema).
The PaymentIntent schema has ~45 properties; only ~20 representative core fields are captured here.
Nested request objects (automatic_payment_methods, payment_method_data, shipping, transfer_data, etc.) are captured by name/type only, not their full sub-schemas.
Environment name is not stated: `servers` gives only the url https://api.stripe.com/
`customer` is anyOf [string, customer, deleted_customer]; no single type is stated
`payment_method` is anyOf [string, payment_method]; no single type is stated
`latest_charge` is anyOf [string, charge]; no single type is stated
`next_action` is anyOf [payment_intent_next_action]; no single type is stated
